cz_intro_1: Then the Dimming: they went dark.
cz_intro_2: Ships jump blind, isle to isle.
cz_intro_4: Relight the Beacons. The Echo waits.
cz_cx_costellatori_b: The Keepers gave them that name; nobody knows what they called themselves. They built the Beacons and mapped the stars as threads of light stretched between them. Their cities stand empty, their script survives on ruins and on the inner faces of the spires. They were gone before the lights went out.
cz_cx_dimming_b: About nine centuries ago the Beacons failed one by one, all within a single generation. Ships already under way never arrived. The network broke into islands, trade became smuggling, and the charts filled with blank space. Nobody knows why it happened. Every faction you will meet was born in that dark.
cz_cx_beacon_dead_b: Up close a dead Beacon is a cliff of frosted crystal, cracked along its facets, its metal rings stopped mid-turn. Instruments read it as cold, but not empty. Keeper shuttles still dock at its base and leave candles burning in the windows, for whoever might be watching.
cz_cx_beacon_dead_h: Visit a system with a dark Beacon.
cz_cx_beacon_lit_b: A Beacon is not a lamp. It is a held breath of space: a fixed point that lets a ship jump without drifting into the dark. Its rings turn, its heart burns white and gold, and the thread to the next Beacon shows on every chart in range. Pilots slow down to look at it, even the ones running late.
cz_cx_beacon_lit_h: Visit a system with a lit Beacon.
cz_cx_relight_b: It takes three things. A relic, a crystal from a Costellatori ruin, seated in the Beacon's heart. A pilot to carry it there. And time: minutes of charge while the spire wakes and everything nearby takes notice. When it lights, a route opens. And something answers.
cz_cx_voice_b: First it was interference on every channel at once. Then the interference had a rhythm. Then words, few and carefully chosen, in an accent nobody can place. The Voice asks questions and seldom answers them. It seems to listen less to what you answer than to how.
cz_cx_echo_fleet_b: When the Echo stops talking, it sends ships. They unfold out of relit Beacons, made of the same lattice: shards, interceptors, slow chandeliers of light. They fly in perfect formation and fire in patterns that sound like music over the comms. They are beautiful. Don't stop to watch.
cz_cx_graveyard_b: Around a swollen red star drift hundreds of hulls of every age: ships that were mid-jump when the Dimming came and fell out wherever they could. The Wrecks cut them open one plate at a time. Some still hold air. A few still hold their crews, and those the Wrecks leave alone.
cz_cx_deep_b: Past the third sector the charts go thin. The stars are older, redder, further apart, and the Beacons follow a pattern seen nowhere else. Distances feel longer than the instruments say. Pilots who come back from out here tend to talk less.
cz_cx_warden_b: Something the size of a moon keeps the oldest sector: black crystal under a slow crown of rings, a single white core burning like an eye. It guards the place where the Dimming began. It does not look like a ship built to attack. It looks like a door that was locked from the inside.
cz_cx_beyond_b: From the last lit Beacon the galaxy is a bright spiral at your back, and ahead there is nothing: no stars, no dust, no signal. The sensors return a shape anyway, too large to measure, outlined in faint red. Nothing out there moves. Nothing out there needs to.
cz_cx_truth_b: Mother Ilse read it twice before she would say it aloud. The Costellatori were not victims of the Dimming. They caused it, Beacon by Beacon, to hide the galaxy from something beyond its edge. A Beacon shines both ways. Every light you have relit can be seen from out there.
cz_cx_gilda_b: The merchant houses that survived the Dimming by owning the few routes still lit. Their convoys are the arteries of the sector, their patrols keep them flowing, and their law holds wherever it pays. The Guild wants the Beacons relit, and owned. It pays well and keeps the receipts.
cz_cx_custodi_b: A monastic order that has tended the dead Beacons for nine centuries without understanding them. They read the Costellatori script badly and pray to it well. They protect relics and pay for them, and distrust anyone who sells them. Their fighters never chase far from what they guard.
cz_cx_relitti_b: Salvagers, pirates, and the families who live in the hulls the Dimming left stranded. Not evil: free. They strip what the Guild abandons, raid what it hoards, and know paths no chart shows. Every ship they fly was once part of three others.
cz_cx_eco_b: It answers when a Beacon is relit: first as interference, then as a voice, then as ships of lattice. The Keepers call it a ghost, the Guild a fault, the Wrecks bad luck. It may be the network itself, left on guard. It weighs the pilots who relight: the patient it speaks to, the greedy it fights.
cz_cx_ardali_b: The Guild's great ring of ivory and brass, high above a blue ocean world. Under its domes brokers sell cargo that has not been mined yet, and lanes of small ships flow in and out of the docks day and night. Vesna Ardali runs the floor. Her name is on the station, and on your debt.
cz_cx_lamp_b: Built of white stone into the flank of Lumen, a Beacon dead for nine centuries. The Keepers live in its shadow and pray toward its dark heart, where faint veins of gold still run through the crystal. Mother Ilse lights a candle there every night. She says Lumen is not dead, only waiting.
cz_cx_gutterdeep_b: A hulk-town inside the gutted freighter Patience, stranded by the Dimming and never moved since. Its breaches are patched with scrap and lit by orange lamps; smaller wrecks hang off it on chains. Inside: stalls of engine parts, cooking smoke, children, and Mara Okonkwo, who decides who stays.
cz_cx_gate_b: A gate of pale stone on a rocky plain, taller than any ship that could land beside it. Star charts and threads are carved around its arch. It leads nowhere you can walk to, yet a faint gold light still pulses inside it, slow as breathing. Brother Nilo thinks it was a map you could step into.
cz_cx_gate_h: Walk the ruins of a Costellatori world.
cz_cx_archive_b: A vast hall underground, shelf after shelf of crystal tablets that glow as a lantern passes. Thousands of them, written in the script of the Beacons. Most are star charts. Some are lists of names. One wall was written last, in a hurried hand, and the Keepers have never finished reading it.
cz_cx_archive_h: Walk the ruins of a Costellatori world.
cz_cx_observatory_b: A ruined dome on a peak above a sea of clouds. Its great lens is cracked but still aimed at the same patch of sky, past a nebula, toward the edge of the galaxy. Whoever worked here left in a hurry and left the instruments running. Some of them still are.
cz_cx_observatory_h: Walk the ruins of a Costellatori world.
cz_cx_w_rocky_b: Mesas, canyons, thin air, often two or three moons. Rocky worlds were the Costellatori's favourite ground: most of their ruins stand on stone, half buried in sand, arches carved with star charts. Land near them. The Keepers pay for what you find, and the Wrecks pay more.
cz_cx_w_rocky_h: Scan a rocky world from orbit.
cz_cx_w_desert_b: Copper dunes under a white sun, heat that bends the horizon. The sand hides things: fossil ribs of animals nobody has seen alive, and ships that came down in the Dimming. Caravans of hover-sleds cross the dunes for salvage. Below the dune line, keep your intakes closed.
cz_cx_w_desert_h: Scan a desert world from orbit.
cz_cx_w_ocean_b: Sea from pole to pole, with rain crossing it in curtains. Floating islands of coral glow at dusk, and where the water runs shallow, harbours stand on stilts. Ocean worlds feed half the sector, and the Guild knows it: its grain contracts are signed here.
cz_cx_w_ocean_h: Scan an ocean world from orbit.
cz_cx_w_ice_b: Blue glaciers, ice spires, green and violet auroras over a long night. Under the ice some Costellatori monuments have kept better than anywhere else, frozen in mid-sentence. Expeditions go down with heaters and come back with frostbite and a few relics.
cz_cx_w_ice_h: Scan an ice world from orbit.
cz_cx_w_jungle_b: Spiral trees taller than towers, fruit that glows teal in the mist, winged things that follow your ship out of curiosity. Overgrown stairs of pale stone climb toward temples nobody has reached. Life here grows fast and covers everything, ruins included.
cz_cx_w_jungle_h: Scan a jungle world from orbit.
cz_cx_w_volcanic_b: Lava rivers under basalt cliffs, ash storms threaded with lightning. Nobody lives here for the view. Mining outposts cling to the cliff edges and pay double, and their ore keeps the sector's shipyards working. Land on the windward side, or not at all.
cz_cx_w_volcanic_h: Scan a volcanic world from orbit.
cz_cx_w_gas_b: No ground, only storm bands deep enough to swallow a planet. Above them float the Guild's cloud cities, great discs held up by engines, harvester ships trailing vapour behind them. The richest houses live here, above the weather and, they will tell you, above everything else.
cz_cx_w_gas_h: Scan a gas giant from orbit.
cz_cx_w_crystal_b: Worlds the Echo has touched slowly turn to lattice. Hills, trees and lakes keep their shapes, but in crystal veined with cyan light; shards float above the water. It is silent and beautiful, and nobody knows if it can be undone. Instruments drift here, and pilots who stay too long come back quieter.
cz_cx_w_crystal_h: Scan a crystal world from orbit.
cz_cx_s_courier_b: Your ship: a stubby courier with two swivelling engine pods, a big cargo hatch and olive paint patched more times than you remember. Not built to fight, but she turns tight and forgives mistakes. Four missiles, three flares. Treat her well: she is the only thing you own outright, and even she is collateral.
cz_cx_s_lancer_b: A needle of ivory and blue with a single engine: the Guild's standard patrol fighter, flown in disciplined wings. Fast and well flown, but lightly shielded. Don't race it in a straight line. Break hard, let it overshoot, and finish it before its wingmen close up.
cz_cx_s_bastion_b: Wide, armoured and slow to turn, with twin heavy cannons and a pair of missiles. The Guild sends Bastions when Lancers aren't enough. Never trade fire with one head-on. Get on its tail and stay there: it cannot turn fast enough to follow you.
cz_cx_s_warden_b: A collared corvette that escorts the richest convoys. Turrets above and below, a shield generator on its back. Kill the generator first, keep the hull between you and the turrets, then go for the bridge near the stern: that is its weak point.
cz_cx_s_hauler_b: A train of cargo pods behind a single engine block, loaded with everything the sector needs. Haulers carry no guns and rely on their escort. When you escort them, watch for boarders. When you hunt them, the engines are the only target that matters.
cz_cx_s_hauler_h: Meet a Guild hauler in battle.
cz_cx_s_scrapwing_b: One pod, one big patched wing, one roaring engine and no shields at all. Scrapwings are cheap and come in swarms, often launched from a Hulk's belly. A short burst kills one. The danger is the next six: keep moving and never fight them in a straight line.
cz_cx_s_harpoon_b: A forked bow with a glowing emitter between the tines. A Harpoon fires a tether, holds you on a leash and sits behind you while its friends close in. The moment it catches you, boost to tear free, then turn and kill it before it casts the line again.
cz_cx_s_gutter_b: A drill nose, an armoured hull and no guns at all. Gutters don't fight: they latch onto haulers and stations and cut their way in. Shoot them on approach, before they reach the hull. If they have already latched on, you can still pick them off the plating.
cz_cx_s_hulk_b: A freighter from before the Dimming, welded over with plates, spikes and improvised turrets. No shields, a great deal of armour and a belly full of Scrapwings. Silence the turrets on your side, then dive for the reactor in the aft section: that is its weak point.
cz_cx_s_votive_b: A white-stone spindle inside a halo wing, lit in gold. Votives fly in pairs around relics and barges, with stronger shields than their size suggests. They never chase far. Draw them away from what they guard, wear the shields down, then finish the hull.
cz_cx_s_censer_b: A long white hull with green-gold filigree and small banners on its masts. Censers stand off and lob slow homing torpedoes at capital ships, stations and you. The torpedoes can be shot down. Do that first, then close in: up close, a Censer turns like a cathedral.
cz_cx_s_reliquary_b: A cathedral that flies. The Keepers carry their relics in it, ringed by point-defence turrets, with a shield generator forward of the bell tower. The bridge is the bell tower itself. Strip the shields, stay out of the turrets' arcs, and toll the bell.
cz_cx_s_shard_b: A dark crystal heart in three blades of lattice, small enough to hide behind a hauler's antenna. Shards come in swarms that move like a single thought. Each one dies to a short burst. Fight them from the edge of the swarm, never from the middle.
cz_cx_s_lattice_b: A crystal lance that changes shape in flight. When your fire comes close it phases out, blinks sideways and reappears on your flank. Don't hold the trigger down: fire short bursts where it is about to be, and keep your rear shield up.
cz_cx_s_choir_b: A slow chandelier of lattice, bigger than a gunship. It restores the shields of every Echo ship near it and sings chords of slow bolts you can see coming. While it sings, the others will not die. Kill it first, whatever else is shooting at you.
cz_cx_c_pilot_b: You. Late thirties, grey coming in at the temples, an olive flight jacket with a courier patch faded almost to nothing. Independent, which mostly means alone and in debt. Ren has carried other people's cargo across half the sector, and still cuts the engines to look at a nebula.
cz_cx_c_broker_b: Silver chignon, a brass monocle over the left eye, an ivory coat that has never met grease. She gave you your first contract and she holds your debt. Vesna is never cruel and never generous. She puts a price on everything, people included, and she is usually right.
cz_cx_c_admiral_b: Commander of the Guild patrols: broad, white-bearded, a scar across his right cheek. Raske believes the Beacons are too important to belong to anyone but the Guild. He keeps his promises exactly, word for word, and not one step further.
cz_cx_c_abbess_b: Abbess of the Keepers: very old, a hood of grey wool, gold glyphs tattooed on her forehead, her left eye clouded. She reads the Costellatori script better than anyone alive. She is calm about almost everything. When she isn't, pay attention.
cz_cx_c_novice_b: Ilse's novice: a teenager with a shaved head, freckles and a robe two sizes too big. He carries a small crystal lantern that glows near Costellatori stone, and he is your guide to the ruins. He asks a question at every step. Most of them are good ones.
cz_cx_c_matriarch_b: Head of the Gutterdeep families. Braids tied with copper wire, welding goggles pushed up, a left arm she built herself from salvage. Mara fixes ships, settles feuds and decides who eats when the market runs thin. She doesn't trust the Guild. She might trust you.
cz_cx_c_mechanic_b: Sixteen, red hair in a messy bun, grease on both cheeks, orange coveralls rolled at the cuffs, a wrench on her shoulder. Mara's mechanic, and the reason your ship still flies. Pip talks to engines more politely than to people. The engines seem to appreciate it.
cz_cx_c_mechanic_h: Buy an upgrade at a Wrecks yard.
cz_cx_c_echo_b: A face made of cyan and violet lines, with two bright points for eyes. It rises out of the static on your comms screen and speaks for the Echo. It says “we”, it asks why, and it remembers what you did the last time.
cz_cx_c_ace_gutter_b: Wiry, crooked grin, gold tooth, a cracked red helmet under her arm and kill marks painted all over her fighter. The most wanted pirate ace in the sector, and proud of the figure on her bounty. She fights dirty, laughs on open channels, and has never stayed caught for long.
cz_cx_c_ace_gutter_h: Cross paths with her in a bounty hunt.
cz_cx_c_ace_lancer_b: The Guild's finest pilot: young, chiselled, visor up, uniform immaculate. Oren has never lost a duel and considers you a rounding error. He flies by the book, and he wrote half of it. Beat him and the Guild will remember your name, for better and for worse.
cz_cx_c_ace_lancer_h: Cross paths with him in a bounty hunt.
cz_cx_c_ace_bram_b: A big old smuggler in a long grey coat, leather eyepatch, tattooed knuckles. Bram knows routes that were dark before the Dimming, and sells them dear. Some days he flies against you, some days beside you. Either way, he asks after your health.
cz_cx_c_ace_bram_h: Cross paths with him in a bounty hunt.
cz_cx_c_ace_vigil_b: A Keeper warrior pilot in white-gold armour, shaved head, calm grey eyes. She escorts relics and the people who carry them. Vigil prays before she fights, and hurries neither. Ask her about forgiveness and she will tell you the Lamp forgives. She does not.
cz_cx_c_ace_vigil_h: Cross paths with her in a bounty hunt.

cz_c_relight_start: The relic is seated. Now hold the light, child, and don't let it fall.
cz_c_relight_half: Halfway. Listen: the spire is starting to hum.
cz_c_relight_raiders: Smell that? A relic aboard that courier. Take it, and take the ship too.
cz_c_relight_hold: Keep them off the spire. Nothing touches it until it burns.
cz_c_relight_burst: Look. Look at it. Nine hundred years of dark, and it still remembers.
cz_c_voice_calm_0: You waited. Few wait. We are measuring you.
cz_c_voice_calm_1: Small ship. Slow hands. Good. Go on.
cz_c_voice_calm_2: Every light you make is a word. Choose them.
cz_c_voice_warn_0: Too many lights. Too fast. You are shouting.
cz_c_voice_warn_1: Stop. A light is seen from very far away. Stop.
cz_c_voice_warn_2: We weighed you. You are hungry. We are coming.
cz_c_voice_sector: This sector sings again. Deeper in, a door opens. Walk, small ship.
cz_c_echo_leave: They're pulling back. Weapons cold. They were only looking at us.

cz_c_found_archive: An archive! The tablets glow when the light passes. Mother Ilse would give an eye to read them.
